justifications.decision: The first pāda is not merely a general statement that action matters; Śaṅkara explicitly construes “karmaṇy eva adhikāraḥ te” as “your adhikāra is only in action,” and adds the exclusion “not in steadfastness in knowledge.”
options_considered: “You have authority only over action,” with eva restricting karmaṇi
“You have authority over action also,” taking eva weakly
“You have authority over action and knowledge alike”
justifications.chosen: adhikāra is restricted to karma, with eva excluding jñāna-niṣṭhā

evidence.quote: karmaṇy evādhikāro na jñāna-niṣṭhāyāṃ te tava |
evidence.translation: Your adhikāra is only in action, not in steadfastness in knowledge.

justifications.decision: The enclitic te is taken as genitive singular, not dative, because the commentary twice glosses te with tava.

evidence.translation: Let there not be your attachment to non-action.

justifications.decision: The second clause has an ellipsis: Śaṅkara supplies adhikāro ’stu with phaleṣu and further explains it as the absence of karma-phala-tṛṣṇā, thirst for the fruit of action, in any state whatsoever.
options_considered: supply adhikāraḥ/astu: “let there be no entitlement over fruits”
take phaleṣu independently: “do not act among fruits”
read it only as a ban on receiving results, not on craving them
justifications.chosen: mā phaleṣu means ‘let there be no adhikāra over the fruits,’ i.e. no craving for action-results

evidence.quote: tatra ca karma kurvataḥ mā phaleṣu adhikāro 'stu, karma-phala-tṛṣṇā mā bhūt kadācana kasyāṃcid apy avasthāyām ity arthaḥ |
evidence.translation: And there, while you perform action, let there be no adhikāra over the fruits; the meaning is: let there be no craving for the fruit of action ever, in any condition at all.

justifications.decision: The compound is not treated merely as ‘one whose motive is fruit.’ Śaṅkara explains that if thirst for the fruit arises, one becomes the hetu of karma-phala-prāpti; action prompted by that thirst makes one the cause of the fruit of action, namely birth.
options_considered: agent who produces ordinary visible results only
justifications.chosen: karma-phala-hetuḥ is ‘cause of obtaining the fruit of action,’ especially the fruit that is birth

evidence.quote: yadā karma-phale tṛṣṇā te syāt tadā karma-phala-prāpter hetuḥ syāḥ, evaṃ mā karma-phala-hetuḥ bhūḥ |
evidence.translation: When thirst for the fruit of action would be yours, then you would be the cause of obtaining the fruit of action; thus, do not become the cause of the fruit of action.

evidence.quote: yadā hi karma-phala-tṛṣṇā-prayuktaḥ karmaṇi pravartate tadā karma-phalasyaiva janmano hetur bhavet |
evidence.translation: For when one proceeds in action impelled by thirst for the fruit of action, then one would become the cause of birth itself, which is the fruit of action.

justifications.decision: The last prohibition is directed against attachment to not acting. Śaṅkara glosses akarmaṇi as akaraṇe and saṅga as prīti; he frames it against the mistaken thought that if fruit is not desired, painful action should be abandoned.
options_considered: saṅga = mere physical contact rather than attachment/fondness
justifications.chosen: akarmaṇi means ‘in non-performance,’ and saṅga is ‘attachment/fondness’

evidence.quote: yadi karma-phalaṃ neṣyate, kiṃ karmaṇā duḥkha-rūpeṇa ? iti mā te tava saṅgo 'stv akarmaṇi akaraṇe prītir mā bhūt ||bhgs_2.47||
evidence.translation: If the fruit of action is not desired, what is the use of action, which is of the nature of pain? Thinking thus, let there not be your attachment to non-action, to non-performance; let there be no fondness for it.

one_shot_delta: A commentary-blind rendering might take “only over action” as a generic ethic of action, missing Śaṅkara’s explicit exclusion of jñāna-niṣṭhā in this context.

It might translate “do not be karma-phala-hetuḥ” as only “do not be motivated by results”; Śaṅkara instead explains becoming the cause of obtaining action-fruit, ultimately birth, through fruit-craving.
It might take akarmaṇi as ‘inaction’ in an abstract philosophical sense or as ‘bad action’; Śaṅkara glosses it concretely as akaraṇa, non-performance, and saṅga as prīti, fond attachment.
analyzer_disagreements: ByT5 reports te only as tvad_SG, without explicit case or gender. Śaṅkara’s te tava at lines 1 and 5 fixes the case as Ṣaṣṭhī singular; masculine is supplied contextually from Arjuna as addressee, while the form itself remains gender-common.

The verifier reported tool_error/unsupported for karma-phala-hetuḥ as a tatpuruṣa compound. This is not taken as a grammatical rejection: the whole compound stem karma-phala-hetu is required by the instructions, and Śaṅkara’s karma-phala-prāpter hetuḥ supports the tatpuruṣa vigraha.
